capabilities: Sync the vault to a Git remote automatically after edits and on a schedule
Commit, merge and push silently without popups
Preserve both local and remote versions when a conflict occurs
Manage ignore paths in a marked .gitignore block from settings
Inject a Personal Access Token into HTTP headers via a temporary Git config
disambiguation: Not a full Git client; it has no source control, history or diff views and only syncs in the background.
extras: Desktop only; syncing is disabled on mobile at load time, with a documented Termux/cronie workaround for Android. Warns not to run alongside obsidian-git on the same repository to avoid index corruption.
intentEvidence: Goal | Frictionless background backup | A complete Git client experience
motivation: The README states the goal is frictionless background backup rather than a complete Git client experience.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in Git-based vault sync, and existing Git plugins interrupt with popups, manual conflict resolution and heavy source-control views.

relations.evidence: Do not enable both at once — they would operate on the same repository concurrently

summary: Background Git sync that silently commits, merges and pushes the vault to a remote after edits stop and on a fixed interval.
